segments.title: Grey Goose's survival as a houseboat
segments.summary: In 2020, Grey Goose was the sole surviving Steam Gun Boat, altered by her postwar conversion to a houseboat in Kent.
segments.body: In 2020, Grey Goose was the only surviving Steam Gun Boat, although none remained in its wartime form. J. Samuel White built her at Cowes. She was sold around 1957, converted into a houseboat, and moored at Hoo St Werburgh in the Medway district of Kent. Her survival left open the hope that she might someday be restored to her wartime appearance.

evidence.note: The transcript discusses the lack of a preserved Steam Gun Boat and Grey Goose's survival as a houseboat, giving her builder, approximate sale date, Medway location, and hoped-for restoration.

segments.title: Seven Steam Gun Boats completed, one lost
segments.summary: The Royal Navy completed seven Steam Gun Boats and lost one. Grey Fox was offered for sale in October 1947 and appears to have been scrapped.
segments.body: Grey Fox was offered for sale in October 1947 and appears to have been scrapped. Her fate contrasts with Grey Goose's survival in converted form. The Royal Navy ordered many Steam Gun Boats, yet only seven were completed and one was lost. These figures show how far the completed programme fell short of the original intention.

evidence.note: The transcript discusses Grey Fox, seven completed boats, and one loss.

segments.title: Steam Gun Boats against the E-boat threat
segments.summary: Fairmile boats and the larger, costlier Steam Gun Boats were two Royal Navy responses to the E-boat threat.
segments.body: The Royal Navy pursued Fairmile boats and Steam Gun Boats in response to the E-boat threat. Steam Gun Boats were the larger, more expensive option, but the design was viable. Prefabrication was meant to support construction in far greater numbers, though that expansion never took place. The boats that entered service performed well. In this assessment, they were the Second World War type closest to the older torpedo-boat-destroyer concept.

evidence.note: The transcript contrasts Fairmiles and Steam Gun Boats, explains the planned prefabrication, and assesses their service record.
